title: Safety-relevant processing element replacement driven by obsolescence
engineering_question: A safety-relevant electronic component must be replaced because of obsolescence. What safety work is required and can the existing evidence be reused?
one_liner: A component must be replaced for lifecycle reasons. Determine the engineering and safety consequences.
initial_input: Engineering change ECR-011 replaces a safety-relevant processing element with its successor device following an end-of-life notification from the semiconductor supplier.
expected_impacted_domains: Functional safety at the highest allocated integrity level
Supplier qualification of the successor device
Cybersecurity implications of a changed processing element
expected_reasoning_paths: TR-038 passes but was executed on the incumbent device, so safety evidence for an ASIL D requirement is not transferable to a different processing element
TR-037 not_run means the diagnostic coverage analysis required by REQ-082 has not started, which is the critical path item
TR-036 already fails the performance requirement REQ-083 on the prototype, so there is a performance problem in addition to the unstarted safety work
DOC-015 is still draft and explicitly records the outstanding safety element analysis, so the change is not ready for approval
known_unknowns: The successor device safety manual and assumed diagnostic coverage are not in the environment
Last time buy date and available inventory are not represented
Whether the successor device changes the cybersecurity attack surface is not assessed
data_classification: SIMULATED ENTERPRISE ARTEFACT - not OEM, customer or proprietary data
